en: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One Gaṅgī! Kāli kāli mahākāli hrīṃ svāhā!
[This] mantra for subduing frogs and leeches: one should smear the root of the *vadirā* tree upon the hand and foot. Oṃ, the paralyzer! Agni hūṃ! Great paralyzer! Agni paralyzer hūṃ phaṭ!
Hanumantakara-ājñā hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mantra for paralyzing fire. It is an extremely secret application.
The Goddess said:
O Great Lord, I have heard the extensive teachings on mantras, tantras, and so forth;
by your grace, O Lord of the Gods, all of that has been fully comprehended by me.
Now I wish to hear about the Trailokyavijaya [Tantra].
O Lord of Heroes, may I know it so that it may become free from doubt.
O Lord, speak in brief for the benefit of practitioners:
[of] the Goddess who bestows all siddhis and is saluted by gods and asuras. Tha.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Fierce, laughing fiercely with a terrible roar, fanged, with a fearsome face, fleshless, with blood-red eyes, her eyebrows knit in a frown, and smeared with blood and fat.

I bow to her who has the color of a dark blue cloud, whose fleshless lower throat jingles with a most resonant ringing sound, who is the conqueror of the world through the intense resonance of the syllables "Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ," and who possesses a wrathful form.
Listen, O Goddess, with attention; I shall speak to you without doubt:
the goddess Trailokyavijayā is the destroyer of the faction of enemies.
She is the subduer of wicked Khākhodas, the destroyer of fear and poverty,
the pacifier of all misfortune, and the annihilator of sorcery and the like.
She should be known as the Cintāmaṇi, the bestower of happiness and good fortune; the Goddess who grants both worldly enjoyment and liberation is extracted by means of the grid (prastāra).
In a well-recommended region of land, filled with the materials required for one's lineage,
one should there worship a single maiden who is virtuous and possesses auspicious marks.
Having requested permission and being well-composed, the practitioner who knows the ritual procedure should,
O Dear One, extract the previously mentioned arrays of the sword according to the prescribed method.
O sinless one, when the mantras are not held by means of the *prastāra*, they become utterly pure;
therefore, I shall now extract them from the midst of the *prastāra*.
Having first extracted the Tāraka syllable, and immediately after that the Vāgbhava;
[then] Yakṣiṇī mounted upon Raudrī, conjoined with Māheśvarī.
The third seed-syllable is extracted as the drop of the moon (*indubindu*) presided over by *kalā*;
O friend Kubjikā, the sixth is Oḍyāṇa and Pulindikā.
The seven-syllable mantra is proclaimed as being joined with Ḍākinī, Yakṣiṇī, Vahni, and Kaumāri, and distinguished by the peak of Kalā.
Mātaṅgī is exclusively the left [vowel] joined with Bhīṣaṇa;
Kubjikā is Pūrṇapīṭha, and Sākinī should be extracted [therefrom].
Mitrīśa is pervaded by Ruru, and Ṣaṣṭhīśa is conjoined with the Bindu.
Lākinī, Khiṅkhinī, Raudrī, and Kūṣmāṇḍī, pierced by Ruru.
O Supreme Goddess, Ratnasundarī should be divided by Ruru;
Kubjī is joined with Māheśvarī, while Vāmā and Sākinī are separate.
Oḍyāṇa (Oḍīśa) and Mitranātha, together with Raudrī and Kapālin;
and Vāmā and Yakṣiṇī, the second pair joined with Osa.
One should extract Pūrṇapīṭha, which is situated in Raudrī, joined with Raudrī (Ruru) Kaumāri,
and presided over by Kapāliśa and Pulindīśa.
Ambikā is indeed Rūḍhayakṣī, who is sixfold as divided by Ruru;
this has been told, O Goddess of the gods, and thereafter [is described] Raudrī alone.

The letter *ha* ending, preceded by *ṇa*, is combined with the letter *pa*; it is modified by the vowel *e*. The letter *ya* ending, situated after *ṇa*, is likewise divided; and the letter *ra* ending is situated at the end of *ha*.
One should pierce the auspicious *śu* with *ru*, and when it has become twofold, one should extract it;
likewise, the end of *ha* and the end of *va* are pierced by the noose (*pāśa*) and [joined] with the sound *ni*.
O observer of good vows, repeat twice the mantra ending in *māva-stha-hānta-caṇḍa*;
the word *vidyujjihve* follows, with *ṣādhamā* situated below *caṇḍaga*.
O Dear One, having extracted forty-nine syllables from Vīramātṛkā, one should divide that into two parts; thus the first [mantra] has been described.
One should perform the dissolution (pādi) conjoined with the piercing (ruruyuta), and the emergence (hādhaga) conjoined with the entrance (bhādha).
Having performed the absorption (mūrcchita) of the withdrawal (saṃhāra), one should extract the supreme syllable.
Trampled by one holding a skull aloft, split the *sādha* into two;
and with the *goṇasa* in the *bharaṇa*, the *ruru* is firmly situated below.
Having performed the display twice, one should lift [the breath] up in the posture of the divine recliner.

The word *pada* with the letter *ṇa* below it and the vowel *ha*, followed by *ra*, should be joined with the *saṃhāra* and *mūrchita*; indeed, that very [mantra] is [formed] even without the *vidu*. One should utter twice the three-syllabled mantra consisting of *ha* alone and *rā*.
One should write the word "mahāraudrī" and the word "sārdra";
one should extract the word "gajavarma" and the word "chada."
O Goddess worshipped by heroes, perform the repetition twice as "vijṛmbhe," then utter the words "nṛtya nṛtyā śilatā ca dhāriṇī."
The fifty-nine letters are declared to be the two sections;
[the words] "with the knitting of the brows" (*bhṛkuṭītaṭāṭopa*),
"having a face made uneven," and "with limbs smeared with great blood, fat, and marrow."
One should extract the pair of Kaha-s, the pair of Hasa-s, and the pair of Kruddha-s.
Furthermore, upon a dark blue cloud-colored [ground], there is a garland of men;
it flashes in two ways within the *bharaṇa* [mudrā], and likewise, the word "Ghaṇṭārava" is the step.
The word "kīrṇadehā" (with scattered limbs), the word "priya" (dear) joined with "vasāmāṃsa" (fat and flesh),
and below that, "vāmā" (the left one) joined with "eyuta" (separated).
O lady of excellent hips, it has become twofold; O beloved, the syllables are deficient.
The third section has been explained; now listen to the fourth.
Having extracted the syllable *sā* along with its base (*ṭhā*), that which follows it (*dha*), and the arm (*da*) above that, as well as the solitary arm (*dha*) alone;
thus it is said that the world of the Nāgas, shining and situated within Ambikā, is reached.
Having caused the letter E to be swooned (mūrcchita), one should extract it as the form of Raudrī;
then, having extracted the syllable KA, it is established upon the seat of the Earth.
The *cāru* [syllable] is also below, joined with the *saṃbhinnā*, well-composed, consisting of two syllables;
it is the *nāda*, the *bindu*, and the *mṛgāṅka*, united with the Sun, Moon, and Fire.
One should write the syllable *auraka* joined with the *brāhmī-bindu* (*auṃ*), followed by the word *irahaṃ*.
Then, one should draw in the adversary with the phrase *kṛnta kṛnta*.
One should shake off the repetition twice and extract the pair of voids;
the former is joined with the letter *e*, and the younger brother of Pāṇu (the letter *na*) is situated in the middle of the vowels (*khara*).
Overlaid with the seed-syllable of Indra (Aim), joined with the nasal drop (bindu), and honored by the gods;
having uttered the word "vijṛmbhaṇi," followed by forty syllables ending in "namaḥ."
The fourth section has been declared; one should then draw the *haradruma* (the tree of Hara).
Mounted on the left, one should draw forth the tip of the sword, which has been split in two.
First, Kaumārī joined with the Bindu; then the second [syllable] conjoined with Śṛṣṭi;
then the word "Krodharūpā"; and then "Prajvala"—one should utter these twice.
O Bhīma, O Bhīṣaṇī, and another, pierce, pierce the foot again! O Mahāmāyā, cut, cut! O Karālinī, [utter] the pair "kiṭi"!
O auspicious lady, one should again write the words "mahābhūta" and "mātā," as well as the other words "kharvaduṣṭa" and "nivāriṇī."
This section consists of fifty-two syllables and is extracted in five parts;
one should recite "Jaya" twice and extract "Vijaye" twice.
Furthermore, O auspicious lady, the syllable *ūhamaṃ* is the immutable *phetkārī*, whose deity is Soma;
this word, repeated twice, is difficult even for the gods to attain.

Accompanied by the syllable *vānta* (phaṭ) and joined with *kaumāri*, adorned with the crest of *kalā* (hrīṃ), one should recite this three times with effort; it removes the poison of serpents and spirits.
O Goddess, you who consume all sins, ward off all that is evil, remove all fevers, and bring about the destruction of misfortune and enemies.
O Goddess of the Gods, having taken Śavarī and Īśa, and added Khiṅkhinī with half a mātrā, one should triple it and join it with the wife of Vahni.
O Goddess, the sixth section is declared to consist of twenty-two syllables; O Mistress of the Gods, the total number of syllables in the six sections is three hundred.
It must not be told to just anyone if one desires supreme accomplishment;
it should not be given to one who has not been tested, for it becomes fruitless in the mouth [of such a person].
There would be no accomplishment through one's own grasping, and there would be obstacles at every step;
therefore, having respectfully informed and worshipped the feet of the Guru, [one should proceed].
Having bowed down with a serene mind, O beloved, one should receive it and not otherwise;
for it bestows perfection through recitation, O auspicious lady, even from a single utterance.
O Goddess, by reciting this even once, a noble person obtains the fruit of bathing in all sacred fords and being initiated into all sacrifices; this is the truth, the absolute truth.
Seated upon a lion, she is exceedingly fierce, resembling Nīla and Nārada;
she is terrifying with formidable fangs, tawny-eyed, and has tawny hair standing erect.
With a trembling tongue repeatedly licking her lips like lightning within thick clouds,
she possessed a voice as deep as a thundercloud, six faces, and distorted countenances.
Reddish with eighteen eyes, submerged and resembling the sun,
her interior covered with a network of veins, fleshless, and with a frowning face.
She is protected by the instruments of the *goṇasa* [serpent], adorned with a garland of mortals,
possessing a garland of flames that flickers through the lineage, and is extremely difficult for gods and asuras to behold.
The goddess has eighteen arms and is clad in a leopard skin;
she holds an elephant hide, a discus, a sword, an arrow, a chariot wheel, and a mallet.
In his right hands, he holds a trident, a sacrificial vessel (caru), a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), and a pair of scissors;
and [in his left hands], an elephant hide, a shield, a bow, a mace, and a goad.
In the left hands, there is a noose, a bell, and a threatening gesture, followed by a severed head, respectively;
Mahāsvanā has a garland of bells placed at her waist as a girdle.
With her hands, feet, and throat wide open and emitting a great roar,
she was smeared with profuse blood, fat, and marrow, and was most formidable.
In this way, one should meditate upon the Great Goddess, the Auspicious One who conquers the three worlds,
the knowledge that bestows enjoyment and liberation, victory, and the perfection of the mouth.
There exists no knowledge equal to this in the three worlds;
there is nothing in the triple world, including all that is mobile and immobile, which it does not accomplish.
This most blazing and terrible Pratyaṅgirā Mahākālī exists; she accomplishes for the practitioner whatever he strives to achieve through mere remembrance.
O lady with a vajra-like womb, for him there is no restriction regarding time or occasion, nor meditation, recitation, and so forth; neither a vow nor austerity exists for him.
O Goddess, by reciting it even once, one obtains the desired fruit;
it pacifies all sins and brings about all prosperity and virtues.
She quiets all misfortunes, she crushes all the wicked;
she destroys all fears and faults, and she subdues all poverty.
She is the pacifier of all diseases, the destroyer of all calamities,
the generator of all good fortune, and the bestower of great fortune.
From the moment this auspicious knowledge has been placed upon the ear,
from that time forward it shines everywhere, even within Bhairava.
One who has this [mantra] established in his heart shall effortlessly destroy sins such as the uprooting of a linga; for him, the perfection of mantra shall come to pass.
O Goddess of gods, when a man undertakes this [practice] until its completion, who indeed could fully explain its merit, which is ten millionfold?
O Goddess, by mere remembrance, she accomplishes all tasks and purposes;
the wicked machine and the bolted door are not cut asunder at all.
O lady of beautiful hips, by mere remembrance she causes the world of moving and non-moving beings to melt away;
the practitioner, overwhelmed and afflicted by passion, attains bliss through her embrace.
Thus, O lady of excellent form, she is the kindler of all mystical diagrams (*yantra*).
This is the celebrated Kāmāraṇī-vidyā, the destroyer of worldly existence;
it shines eternally within the hollow of the heart-lotus cakra.
Then Caṇḍeśvarī is remembered as she who has made vibration and non-vibration her own food;
she is the preeminent one within the abode of *vicit* (the piercing), whose fortitude is fully blossoming.
Merely by remembering her, the net of nooses that obscures [reality] is certainly dissolved;
for seventy million mantras have emerged from her body.
She who possesses ten million times ten million counter-mantras is the Mistress of seventy million.
Her power and vigor consist of both manifest and unmanifest prowess.
O Goddess, O Great Mother, it is truly, truly impossible to describe [it all];
I have spoken but a mere fraction, so tell me further of the ritual action.
O Goddess, having meditated upon the *cedru* tree and the rosary as being of a beautiful red color,
one may achieve subjugation and attraction by means of [an image] made from red sandalwood.
O Dear One, having visualized the nectar flowing from within the full moon,
O Goddess, one should recite the mantra with a rosary of pearls.
O Goddess, it brings nourishment and conquers death; there is no other way.
One should meditate on [the mantra] as black in color, using *ariṣṭa* beads for the rosary.
By reciting it, one will swiftly destroy even that which is protected by the thirty gods.
One should meditate on [the deity] of smoky color; by reciting the rosary marked with the serpent-syllable (āḥ), combined with the preceding seed-syllable, one effects expulsion.
One should meditate on [the rosary] as being white in color and made of crystal;
through recitation, it certainly effects both pacifying and enriching rites.
One should meditate upon [the deity] of yellow color, holding a rosary of topaz;
O Goddess, by reciting the mantra joined with the seed-syllable, one causes paralysis—of this there is no doubt.
Having reflected thus, one should recite [mantras] with a rosary of rudrākṣa beads while remaining in a state of composure;
this brings about union with Śiva—this is the truth, the absolute truth, O fair-faced lady.
O Goddess, by reciting it seven times, one obtains the fruit of all sacred fords; there is no doubt about this.
Merely by uttering it once, one destroys even great sin.

One attains the fruit of all sacrifices and obtains the fruit of all initiations; one whose conduct regarding the *samaya* has been impaired is purified by reciting [the mantra] a hundred times. Oh, the majesty of the mantra for one who recites it constantly!
Even without the yoga of dissolution, one becomes equal to the lords of yogis. (Tha)
Now, O lady of excellent hips, I shall again explain the well-ascertained treasury of ritual actions according to the method of the nine seed-syllables.
Aiṃ Caṇḍikā is the staff at the tip of the Śiva-tattva; Hrīṃ is Sadāśiva;
Īśvara is the form of Caṇḍa; Bhrū-vidyā is Caṇḍavatī, and Trūṃ is the mistress of the Māyā-tattva, Krūṃ, who is that Caṇḍā, the leader of the Kula.
Then the goddess Drūṃkāra is in Kalā;
Caṇḍanāyināyikā is in Niyati; Caṇḍogrā is in Prūṃ; and Pracaṇḍā is in Puruṣa with Kṣrūṃ.
In the *prakṛti* [mandala], there is Rudracaṇḍā with the syllable *hrūṃ* in the central square extending to the northeast (Īśāna).

[The goddesses] are red, fair, ruddy, black, blue-lotus colored, white, smoky, joyful, the color of the *japā* flower, pale yellow, and the color of a beautiful head, ending with the color of Īśa (the Lord).
*Sahara-kṣa-ma-la-va-yū*, adorned with a crest upon the head;
this is declared as the nine-syllable mantra in the *Śrī-Jayadrathayāmala*.
In this very context it was said: "O Blessed One, from the Vāgbhava [syllable], ending with Caṇḍikā;
having drawn lines extending east-west and four above those, and from south to north, nine squares will clearly be formed."
One should write the syllables of the nine principles (tattvas) in the squares starting from the center and ending in the northeast;
having performed the placement (nyāsa) beginning with Ugradaṇḍa, one becomes a destroyer of the enemies of ritual action.

*Prakṛti*, *Sādākhya*, and *Īśvara* are used for subjugation (*vaśya*); in the reverse order they are used for inciting enmity (*dveṣaṇa*); *Īśa*, *Vidyā*, and *Māyā* are likewise used for attraction (*varaṇa*), starting with *Caṇḍa*.
From Caṇḍa comes Caṇḍogra; from Lakṣa comes Viparīta;
from Vāraṇa comes Niyati; from Puṃs comes Prakṛti; and from Bhūta comes Āveśa; and so on again.
The primary natures (prakṛtis) have been described here.
She who is the sovereign of the dissolution and emergence of the manifestation of vigor—
this group of six has been described by me, O Kālī, as the lotus known as Saṃjñā, O Mistress of the Gods.

Adorned with twenty parts of the thirty [deities], resplendent with hundreds of excellent maidens as its objects, and endowed with fifty syllables—O Queen of the Gods, this must not be spoken of anywhere. Tha.

[In the Bhairava-śrotas, at the seat of knowledge (vidyāpīṭha), in the Śiraccheda-Jayadrathayāmala Mahātantra, in the twenty-four thousand [verse] work, in the second hexad, this is the thirty-sixth chapter: the ritual procedure for Siddhalakṣmī. || Tha ||
May there be prosperity! Auspiciousness and great glory! Thus.
